Article Title: Muslim clerics distance themselves from Hamid Ansari's ‘Hindu extremism’ remarks; call for harmony
Article Text:
‘We are proud we live in India’: Imam body chief hits back at Hamid Ansari over ‘Hindu extremism’ remarks.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The remarks by former Vice President Hamid Ansari on “Hindu extremism” and the RSS have drawn criticism from Muslim clerics, with All India Imam Association president Maulana Sajid Rashidi saying Muslims should not be made to feel like outsiders in India.Rashidi said people who hold constitutional posts are expected to represent all sections of society and questioned Ansari's decision to speak on such issues after leaving office.Speaking to ANI, Rashidi said Ansari had not made many statements in favour of Muslims while serving as Vice President but had spoken on several such issues after leaving office."Hamid Ansari sahab, when he was Vice President, you did not see many statements from him in favour of Muslims. But after leaving that post, several statements have come from him, and it appears as if he is now presenting himself as a leader of Muslims."Rashidi also said extremism should be judged by whether it promotes hatred against other communities."Extremism becomes wrong when hatred against others comes into it. If someone follows their religion and does not trouble others, that is a different matter," he said.'We are even prouder that we live in India'Rashidi said Muslims had chosen to remain in India during Partition and had contributed to the country."We say with pride that we are Muslims, but we are even prouder that we live in India," he said.He said remarks suggesting that Muslims do not belong in India could create a sense of insecurity within the community. He called on political organisations and leaders to act against statements targeting any community.Rashidi also referred to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's remarks on Hindu-Muslim relations and said calls for communal harmony should be followed by people across communities.Earlier on Sunday, chief Imam of All India Imam Organisation Umer Ahmed Ilyasi also criticised Ansari over his comments on "Hindu extremism".Ilyasi alleged that Ansari's remarks were intended to provoke Muslims and could disturb the social atmosphere."I strongly condemn this statement. Today, Hamid Ansari sahab has remembered Muslims again. When he was in power and held important positions, he was secular. Today, he has remembered Muslims.Ilyasi further alleged that Ansari was trying to regain his standing among Muslims and claimed that his remarks could create tension in society."Muslims are not asking about him, and to improve his image among Muslims, he has made such statements. I feel that somewhere this is a big conspiracy to disturb the atmosphere of the country," Ilyasi said.
Article Summary: All India Imam Association president Maulana Sajid Rashidi says Muslims should not be made to feel like outsiders in India. Rashidi said extremism should be judged by whether it promotes hatred against other communities. Chief Imam of All India Imam Organisation Umer Ahmed Ilyasi also criticised Ansari over his comments. Ilyasi alleged that Ansari was trying to regain his standing among Muslims.

Article Title: Senior journalist Payal Mehta passes away at age of 46; PM Modi, Amit Shah offer condolences
Article Text:
Condolences poured in from across the political spectrum following the passing away of senior journalist Payal Mehta.

NEW DELHI: Senior journalist Payal Mehta, who worked with CNN-News18, died in Mumbai in the early hours of Sunday. She was 46.Mehta was visiting Mumbai when she developed uneasiness around 2 am. She was taken to a hospital, but died before treatment could begin.Senior journalist Sheela Bhatt shared the details in a post on X."On a visit to Mumbai, she developed uneasiness. Around 2 am she was taken to the hospital. Before any treatment could be administered, her pulse went silent".Mehta was known for her work covering Parliament, the government and the BJP. Colleagues and senior political leaders remembered her as a dedicated journalist who closely followed national affairs.Prime Minister Narendra Modi , home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh , Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and several Union ministers expressed condolences following her death."Payal Mehta Ji was a hardworking journalist who remained firmly connected to the ground, bringing a deep understanding of national issues to her reporting," Modi said in a post on X.He added that Mehta would also be remembered for her kindness and the warmth she showed towards others."Her sudden and untimely passing is extremely saddening. My condolences to her family, friends and colleagues. May they find strength in this difficult hour. Om Shanti," he said.Shah described Mehta as a thorough professional who was committed to providing detailed information on a range of issues."I extend my deepest condolences to her grieving family and friends and pray to God to give them the strength to bear this profound pain. Om Shanti," he said in a post on X.Singh said he was deeply shocked by her death and recalled her commitment to the Parliament beat."She has left us far too soon. Payal was an extremely hardworking and dedicated journalist who covered the Parliament beat with great commitment and professionalism," he said.He recalled that Mehta would often remain in Parliament from early morning until late at night during sessions, closely following proceedings."My heartfelt condolences to her family and friends in this difficult hour. May they find the strength to bear this irreparable loss. Om Shanti," he said.Railways and Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw also expressed grief over the death of his "journalist and dear friend Payal Mehta"."Her dedication to reporting was exemplary. Om Shanti," he said.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said he was deeply shocked by the news."Had just attended her father's prayer service a few days ago. Payal used to be as regular as me in Parliament during sessions. She was a true professional journalist. Heartfelt prayers for her departed soul. Om Shanti," Rijiju said.
Article Summary: Senior journalist Payal Mehta died in Mumbai in the early hours of Sunday. She was known for her work covering Parliament, the government and the BJP. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh and several Union ministers expressed condolences.

Article Title: 'Party of comedians & jokers': PM Modi's mimicry at Rahul Gandhi's event draws BJP ire
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Sunday slammed Congress after a comedian mocked Prime Minister Narendra Modi while sharing the stage with leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi at his "Chhatron Ki Goonj" event in Indore.In a social media post on X, Union minister Kiren Rijiju said the Congress has become "a party of comedians and jokers.""Congress Party has become a Party of Comedians & Jokers!" Rijiju said."They are out forever.... RIP," he added.Union education minister Pralhad Joshi also targeted Rahul Gandhi and accused him of stooping to an "absolute nadir of moral bankruptcy.""Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party have stooped to an absolute nadir of moral bankruptcy," Joshi said."Weaponising a student interaction to mock and insult the late mother of PM Modi ji reveals a shocking lack of basic human empathy and political culture," he added.BJP leader CR Kesavan also criticised Rahul, alleging that the Congress leader had shared the stage with individuals who mocked an elderly woman by referring to her as a "setting" and accused the Congress leader of laughing at the remarks."Rahul Gandhi shared the stage yesterday with cheap, vulgar trolls who insulted our Naari Shakti by mocking a frail elderly Mataji as a 'setting'," Kesavan said.Kesavan further alleged that the incident reflected an "uncouth culture" and claimed that such conduct was one of the reasons Rahul Gandhi had failed to connect with the youth.This comes after standup comedian Pulkit Mani shared the stage with Rahul and mimicked PM Modi during student-focused programme.During the 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme in Indore on Saturday, Rahul launched a sharp attack on the government over paper leaks and a host of student grievances.Rahul said the programme aimed to restore the "hope" that students had lost in the education system."We want the hope that was shattered in your hearts to return with renewed vigour. We want you to start believing in education and the system once again," Rahul said.He said curiosity, love and affection, humility, honesty and fearlessness were qualities that define a student, and argued that students who ask questions are essential to building a strong nation."Students do not hate. They treat one another with affection, kindness and mutual respect," the Congress leader said, adding that a genuine seeker of knowledge "cannot be arrogant" and should remain tolerant of differing viewpoints.Earlier, at a Congress event in August, Rahul took swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s foreign policy, suggesting that the PM’s diplomacy is overly associated with hugging foreign leaders.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party have stooped to an absolute nadir of moral bankruptcy. Union minister Kiren Rijiju said the Congress has become "a party of comedians and jokers" BJP leader CR Kesavan alleged that the incident reflected an "uncouth culture" Rahul launched a sharp attack on the government over paper leaks and a host of student grievances.

Article Title: 'Tell us where to come, schools being fixed before our visit': CJP mocks Rajasthan govt

What triggered the CJP-government row?

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) member Ashutosh Ranka took a dig at the Rajasthan government, saying the Bhajan Lal Sharma dispensation released Rs 4,000 crore for 472 schools on the day the "cockraoches entered Udaipur"."And a double coincidence that 30% of these schools happen to be in Udaipur," he posted on X.Mentioning the Ranka's post, another CJP member Sourav Das quipped: "People of Rajasthan, tell us where you want us to come. Government is releasing and fixing places before our visit!"Last month, Ranka alleged that Rajasthan Police was keeping a watch on people entering and leaving his house, hours after the organisation’s team faced a confrontation during its campaign to inspect government schools.In a post on X, Ranka said, “For the last 2 hours, Rajasthan police is surveilling every person going in and out of my house.”He challenged the police to arrest him directly if they wanted to, while insisting that he and his team would continue their campaign.“If Rajasthan Police wants, they can come and directly arrest me. Ranka claimed the assault was coordinated and alleged that some of those involved had been seen with a local BJP MLA before the confrontation. Article Title: 'Delhi a terrifying daily story for women': Rahul, Priyanka slam Amit Shah over teen's gangrape-murder
Article Text:
Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women.

What happened in Delhi case

NEW DELHI: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl in Delhi, with both questioning the authorities over women's safety and demanding accountability for the incident.Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, criticised the Delhi Police and questioned the responsibility of Union home minister Amit Shah, under whose ministry the force functions. He said the teenager was gang-raped and murdered before her body was dumped in an open field, and questioned how the police remained unaware of the crime for days.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi described the incident as a "horrific act of brutality" in the national capital. He also dismissed the idea that Delhi was providing women with a safe environment, saying the city had instead become a source of fear for women."It's unfortunate that Delhi is no longer the capital today; it has become a terrifying daily story for women," he said.Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. He pointed out that the Delhi Police is under the Union home ministry and asked who should ultimately be held responsible for the safety of women in the capital."Amit Shah ji, Delhi Police is under your control. Ultimately, whose responsibility is women's safety?" he said.He also criticised the functioning of the Delhi Police, asking whether its role had been reduced to intimidating ordinary citizens while criminals continued to operate without fear."Or has the job of Delhi Police been reduced to just intimidating and threatening ordinary citizens? Because the criminals are roaming around fearlessly," Gandhi said.Calling for immediate action, the Congress leader demanded that those responsible for the crime be arrested and punished strictly. He also sought accountability for what he described as criminal negligence."The beasts must be arrested immediately, strict action and punishment must be taken, and accountability for this criminal negligence must be fixed," he said.Rahul Gandhi ended his post by linking women's safety to India's wider progress, saying, "India cannot move forward without women's safety."Priyanka Gandhi also raised concerns over the case, saying the crime against the teenager represented an extreme form of brutality. She noted that another minor girl had allegedly been raped just days earlier and questioned whether authorities were taking sufficient responsibility for women's safety."In Delhi, all limits of cruelty were crossed against a 17-year-old girl, and after that, she was brutally murdered. Just a few days earlier, another minor girl was raped," she said in a post on X.Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women. She argued that while there was discussion about women's development, women continued to face violence without what she described as concrete action against perpetrators."No one in the country is willing to take responsibility for women's safety—only empty talk about women's development is offered," she said.She claimed that hundreds of women face atrocities and violence and alleged that victims can struggle to get action from authorities, including the registration of FIRs."Hundreds of women face atrocities and violence, but they cannot hope for concrete action against the perpetrators—FIRs aren't even filed," she said.Priyanka Gandhi also said the issue went beyond the individual case and reflected a wider failure to ensure women's basic rights. She argued that both society and the government had failed to provide women with adequate safety, freedom and equality."Both society and the government have completely failed in granting women their rights to safety, freedom, and equality," she said.A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field, with the police facing questions over the delay in detecting the crime.The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital, with Rahul Gandhi focusing on the Delhi Police's role and its accountability to the Union home ministry.Priyanka Gandhi also referred to another case involving a minor girl that was reported days before the teenager's rape and murder. She used the two incidents to question the wider response to crimes against women.
Article Summary: A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field. The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital. Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl.

Article Title: ‘Returning the bottle’: BJP’s Ravneet Bittu detained after protest near Mann’s convoy

NEW DELHI: BJP leader and former Union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu was detained by Ludhiana Police on Saturday after he protested with eggs and tomatoes as chief minister Bhagwant Mann ’s cavalcade passed through Ludhiana.Bittu was detained by the Ludhiana Police and whisked away to an undisclosed location. He said he had brought the matter to the notice of the Union Home Ministry.Bittu, the grandson of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, was travelling to Pathankot for the anti-drug yatra being launched by BJP president Nitin Nabin. Article Title: ‘Close ties with Crown Prince’: Sri Lankan MP seeks PM Modi’s help for release of Tamil youth accused of blasphemy in Saudi
Article Text:
Anojan Sivarasa's family has claimed that he was sentenced to death over a social media post allegedly amounting to blasphemy

(With PTI inputs)

A Sri Lankan opposition lawmaker on Saturday urged President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to seek Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s intervention in the case of a young Sri Lankan Tamil facing judicial proceedings in Saudi Arabia.In making the appeal, Mano Ganesan, a leader of the Tamil Progressive Alliance, cited PM Modi’s “close ties” with Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman.“I urge President @anuradisanayake to bring #Anojan_Sivarasa’s desperate plight to the urgent attention of your friend, recipient of ‘SriLanka Rathna’ Prime Minister Narendra Modi,” Ganesan wrote on X.“Given PM Modi’s close ties with Saudi Prime Minister and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, I appeal to you to ask PM Modi to personally intervene with Crown Prince Salman and seek a humanitarian resolution for Anojan,” he added.The appeal concerns Sri Lankan national Anojan Sivarasa, whose family has claimed that he was sentenced to death in Saudi Arabia over a social media post allegedly amounting to blasphemy.Sri Lanka’s foreign ministry, however, has not confirmed that Sivarasa has been sentenced to death.Sivarasa, a minority Tamil from Sri Lanka’s Eastern Province, is a resident of Natpittimunai in Kalmunai. He travelled to Saudi Arabia for employment nine months ago.The Sri Lankan ministry of foreign affairs on Friday confirmed that it remains engaged with Saudi authorities over the case.“The ministry remains engaged with the relevant Saudi authorities through diplomatic channels and is taking appropriate steps to safeguard Mr. Anojan Sivarasa’s interests and provide him with all possible assistance,” it said.Sivarasa was initially sentenced to five years in prison and fined three million Saudi riyals after being found guilty of posting social media content deemed insulting to a religion.According to the report, his lawyer later verbally informed the Sri Lankan Embassy in Riyadh that the sentence had reportedly been enhanced to capital punishment.The embassy, however, is awaiting the formal written judgment from Saudi judicial authorities before confirming the development.The lawyer has also informed the embassy that the judgment could be appealed before Saudi Arabia’s Supreme Court within one month. The embassy, in consultation with the ministry, is taking steps to pursue the appeal in coordination with Sivarasa’s family.Sri Lankan Tamils account for around 12-13% of the island nation’s population of more than 20 million and are mainly concentrated in the Northern and Eastern provinces.
Article Summary: Anojan Sivarasa was initially sentenced to five years in prison and fined three million Saudi riyals. His lawyer later verbally informed the Sri Lankan Embassy in Riyadh that the sentence had reportedly been enhanced to capital punishment. The Sri Lanka ministry of foreign affairs on Friday confirmed that it remains engaged with Saudi authorities over the case.

Article Title: ‘We do not operate under pressure from any nation’: Govt on Trump's Russia sanctions law
Article Text:
MoS Kirti Vardhan Singh on Russian sactions

NEW DELHI: India will take decisions in the best interests of its people and will continue to follow an independent foreign policy, minister of state for external affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said while responding to a question on Trump's Russian sanctions law and its possible impact on India.“The people of India are the top priority for our government. We will take every measure that benefits our public,” Singh told news agency ANI.US ​President ⁠Donald Trump ‌signed ‌the ⁠Russia ⁠sanctions ​bill ‌into law, the White ‌House ​said ⁠in a ‌statement. The Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act seeks to impose steep levies on Moscow and its top energy buyers, including India and China.Singh said India does not base its decisions on the dictates of other nations and will take steps to safeguard the country's strength and stability.“We will take decisive steps to ensure the strength and stability of our nation and its population. We maintain an independent foreign policy; we do not align ourselves based on the dictates of other nations but rather act in the best interests of our own country,” he said.He also reiterated India's position on the tariffs being imposed, saying, “We have consistently maintained that the tariffs being imposed are unfair, and we do not operate under pressure from any other nation.”On India's energy needs, Singh said the government would continue to source energy based on what is commercially viable and economical.“Energy is a primary concern for us; we will source energy for our country and our people from wherever we find commercially viable and economical options,” he said.
Article Summary: India will continue to follow an independent foreign policy, minister of state for external affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said. He was responding to a question on Trump's Russian sanctions law and its possible impact on India. Singh said India does not base its decisions on the dictates of other nations.

Article Title: Toll rises to 31 as 22-hour standoff ends at Pakistan police line HQ
Article Text:
What began on Friday as a suicide blast at the compound’s perimeter gate rapidly developed into an active siege

NEW DELHI: The death toll from the attack on the police lines headquarters in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, rose to at least 31, with over 100 injured, as military and police forces concluded the 22-hour-long stand-off Saturday noon.What began on Friday as a suicide blast at the compound's perimeter gate rapidly developed into an active siege after at least seven operatives from the Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP) group breached the counter terrorism department (CTD) and intelligence facilities. In a turn of events, the operatives, once inside, managed to reach the facility's weapons depot, released many detained terror suspects, and armed some of them to fight the Pakistani personnel, sources said.Despite a large deployment, heavy gunfire was exchanged through Friday night and Saturday morning. A military command with the infantry division was used to direct the Pak govt's operation, but strong resistance from inside the lockdown zone prolonged the multi-building standoff, leaving scores wounded and critical.Among those killed were SP Akbar Shinwari, a deputy SP and Dr Israel Orakzai, head of the pediatrics department at Kohat hospital.A few civilians also died in the exchange of fire.Special Service Group (SSG) Zarrar unit and infantry division had to be pressed into service to end the siege and clear the compound. Khyber Police claimed to have neutralised eight of the attackers. The facility, which has been facilitating establishment of new terror camps in KPK region, was struck Friday afternoon with a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED), enabling multiple suicide attackers to force their way inside the premises shooting indiscriminately.
Article Summary: The death toll from the attack on the police lines headquarters in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, rose to at least 31, with over 100 injured, as military and police forces concluded the 22-hour-long stand-off Saturday noon. What began on Friday as a suicide blast at the compound’s perimeter gate rapidly developed into an active siege.

Article Title: ‘Arrogance of power’: Congress calls out Scindia over his viral video with MP residents over road
Article Text:
Union minister's fiery response to Guna resident goes viral, Congress reacts

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A video showing Union minister Jyotiraditya M Scindia in a sharp exchange with a resident over a long-pending road in Guna, Madhya Pradesh, has gone viral on social media, with the Congress sharing the clip and accusing the minister of showing “arrogance of power”.The exchange took place after local residents stopped Scindia’s convoy during his visit and raised concerns over the delayed road work. Residents carrying placards also raised the slogan “Road nahi to vote nahi” (No road, no vote), prompting a tense exchange between the minister and one of the residents.In the video, the resident urges Scindia to ensure the road is completed before the next election and warns that people would otherwise not vote.“This is a request that this road should be laid this time. Otherwise, when you come at the time of voting, we will not vote at all. This entire colony,” the resident says.Scindia objected to the manner in which the demand was made, saying, “Do not ever use this language with me. Understood? I am talking to everyone. You come and make a request. It is my responsibility to get the work done. Okay?”The Congress later shared the video on its official X account, writing, “Look at the arrogance of power.”The party also alleged that Scindia “flew into a rage”. The party added, “The moment the public demanded a road, 'His Majesty' flew into a rage.” It further quoted Scindia’s response and said, “The public will soon put this arrogance in its place.”The video comes amid local complaints over the condition and construction of the road. The confrontation was followed by an announcement on the project.At a public programme later, Scindia announced that Rs 3 crore would be sanctioned for road construction from the MLA’s fund, from the quota of Guna MLA Pannalal Shakya. He also directed the district collector to ensure that work is taken up after the monsoon, according to reports.The episode has since shifted attention from the road demand to the exchange itself, with the viral footage prompting renewed discussion on how elected representatives respond to constituents’ grievances.
Article Summary: Video shows Union minister Jyotiraditya M Scindia in a sharp exchange with a resident over a long-pending road in Guna, Madhya Pradesh. The Congress shared the clip and accused the minister of showing “arrogance of power”

Article Title: Mehbooba, Mirwaiz oppose proposed ‘spiritual’ retreat in J&K, ask CM to step in
Article Text:
Mehbooba Mufti and Mirwaiz Umar Farooq Saturday sought intervention of CM to intervene and stop “Tantra Silence”

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Public representatives and the clergy in J&K have expressed outrage over a proposed four-day “spiritual” event in the scenic Gurez Valley being organsied by a self-styled godman whose similar event in Goa last year was cancelled after its allegedly obscene promotional material sparked widespread controversy.Former J&K CM and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti and Hurriyat Conference chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq Saturday sought intervention of CM Omar Abdullah to intervene and stop “Tantra Silence” retreat from being held.“A poster is advertising a “Tantra Silence” retreat in Gurez Valley, Srinagar. A similar ‘Tantra‘ retreat facilitated by Swami Dhyan Sumit, a self-styled godman promoting a new religion under the Shree Rajneesh Foundation, was cancelled in Goa last year after its obscene promotional material sparked widespread controversy and the Goa Police had to intervene. Gurez is no playground for experiments in the name of spirituality or tourism. ,” Mehbooba wrote on X, requesting J&K CM to intervene immediately and take appropriate action.Mirwaiz said, “This kind of programme is being allowed in Gurez in Kashmir, when a similar programme by this organisation was cancelled by police in Goa, due to public outrage over its obscene promotional details, is outrageous.”“Kashmir is the land of sufis and saints. Here, spirituality is experienced, not marketed at a cost! Besides, tourism promotion cannot become an excuse to undermine our religious, cultural and social ethos and ignoring our values and sensibilities,” Mirwaiz said, asking J&K CM to take note and stop what he called “this exploitation.”Mufti Nasir-ul-Islam, the Grand Mufti of Jammu & Kashmir, said he has taken serious note of the proposed “Tantra in Silence” retreat reportedly scheduled for Sept 24-27 in Gurez Valley. “The programme is publicly advertised as a meditation retreat, and concerns regarding its organisers, content and suitability for the region have been raised publicly,” he said, adding that Gurez is not merely a tourist destination. “It is part of the sacred cultural landscape of Kashmir, a land shaped by generations of faith, scholarship and spiritual tradition. Its hospitality must never be understood as indifference to its moral and cultural character,” he said.He said the govt should verify the organisers, examine the complete programme and its promotional material, ascertain the permissions granted, and ensure that no activity contrary to law or the legitimate religious and cultural sensitivities of the people is permitted.Meanwhile, as the matter escalated, the Bandipore district administration issued a statement late Saturday evening that no permission has been granted for the event. “Public/tourists are advised not to rely on or share such unauthorised promotional claims,” the statement said.Bandipora deputy commissioner Indu Kanwal didn’t respond to phone calls.After abrogation of Article 370 in 2019, Gurez valley along the LOC in Bandipora district has emerged Kashmir’s fastest-growing tourist destination witnessing huge tourist rush.
Article Summary: A similar retreat facilitated by Swami Dhyan Sumit, a self-styled godman promoting a new religion under the Shree Rajneesh Foundation, was cancelled in Goa last year after its obscene promotional material sparked widespread controversy. Mehbooba Mufti and Mirwaiz Umar Farooq Saturday sought intervention of CM Omar Abdullah to intervene and stop ‘Tantra Silence’ retreat from being held.

SRINAGAR: Advocate Abu Adil Pandit, representing JKLF chairman Mohammad Yasin Malik in the Kashmiri Pandit nurse Sarla Bhat killing case, Saturday filed an application before a Srinagar court, seeking permission to withdraw his power of attorney and cease representing Malik in the proceedings.In his application, Pandit said Malik, in his written submissions, had stated that he had decided not to contest the trial proceedings further. He described Malik’s submissions as a “reflection of the accused’s personal and conscientious consideration of the course he proposes to adopt in the present proceedings.”In view of that decision and the instructions received from Malik, Pandit said he has no further instructions to continue representing him in the case.He added his application should not be construed as an admission of any fact, allegation, charge, circumstance or contention forming part of the case or as an admission of guilt or acceptance of the allegations against Malik.He also said that his request was confined to the proceedings pending before the court and would not affect separate cases in which he continues to represent Malik.
Article Summary: Advocate Abu Adil Pandit is representing JKLF chairman Mohammad Yasin Malik in the Kashmiri Pandit nurse Sarla Bhat killing case. He has filed an application before a Srinagar court, seeking permission to withdraw his power of attorney and cease representing Malik.

Article Title: J&K crippled by ‘lame duck’ assembly & CM: Former CEC Quraishi
Article Text:
Quraishi stressed that Kashmir needs democracy, reconciliation and revival of its old sense of shared belonging

SRINAGAR: J&K has a “lame duck” assembly and chief minister with limited powers, former chief election commissioner SY Quraishi said Saturday.“What is the meaning of an elected chief minister when representative institutions remain outside his direct control?” Quraishi asked during a lecture in which he also cautioned against “exploiting” Kashmiri Pandits’ killings while arguing that many more Muslims were slain by terrorists.In his address at Mohammad Shafi Pandit Memorial Lecture in Srinagar’s Institute of Engineering, Quraishi stressed that Kashmir needs democracy, reconciliation and revival of its old sense of shared belonging. The lecture was held in the memory of Pandit, the first Muslim IAS officer from Kashmir who passed away on Sept 19, 2024, at age 80.Quraishi noted that Supreme Court had shown “soft-heartedness” towards restoration of J&K’s statehood by observing it should be done “as soon as possible” while upholding Article 370’s abrogation. He pointed out that assembly polls were held in 2024 after a deadline set by Supreme Court, which did not do the same for statehood, prompting the question “for how long”.On Pandits, Quraishi described their displacement as one of Kashmir’s deepest wounds for more than three decades and acknowledged that govt must ensure their security, housing, employment, and confidence.“But ultimately, Pandits cannot truly return merely to govt-built colonies. They must return to Kashmir, to neighbourhoods, friendships, schools, markets and old relationships. A Pandit moving into a protected housing complex is rehabilitation. A Pandit returning to a street, where an old Muslim neighbor knocks on the door and welcomes him back, is reconciliation. It would be the victory of Kashmir over those who sought to destroy its plural spirit,” the former CEC said.
Article Summary: Former chief election commissioner SY Quraishi said J&K has a ‘lame duck’ assembly and chief minister with limited powers. He also cautioned against “exploiting’ Kashmiri Pandits’ killings while arguing that many more Muslims were slain by terrorists.

Article Title: ‘Trapped in dynastic politics, running his own shop’: Mukesh Sahani slams Sanjay Nishad

NEW DELHI: Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP) president Mukesh Sahani on Saturday accused Uttar Pradesh minister and Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad of being "trapped in dynastic politics" and alleged that he had failed to secure reservation for the Nishad community despite being in the government for five years.Sahani, who arrived in Sonbhadra as part of his "Aarakshan Sankalp Yatra", administered an oath to members of the Nishad (Mallah) community, asking them to pledge with Ganga water in hand that they would not vote for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) until their community gets the benefits of reservation.Speaking to reporters, Sahani said the campaign would continue across villages until November 30 to organise Nishad community members and create awareness about their reservation demand.The former Bihar minister said the campaign aims to get 50 lakh people to take the pledge.Targeting the Nishad Party chief, Sahani said, "Sanjay Nishad has got trapped in dynastic politics and, after joining the government, is running his own shop. NEW DELHI: Former vice president Mohammad Hamid Ansari on Saturday cited former prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru 's remarks about the “danger to India” while referring to concerns raised by late constitutional expert and author AG Noorani in his book The RSS : A Menace to India.He was addressing the event, titled “Remembering a Polymath: The Life and Times of Abdul Ghafoor Noorani”, organised at the India Islamic Cultural Centre to commemorate the life and works of the jurist and author.Addressing an event, Ansari recalled jurist and author Abdul Ghafoor Noorani's observations in the introduction to his 2019 book and cited remarks by Nehru that were recorded by former Foreign Secretary Jagat Singh Gundevia during a meeting of Ministry of External Affairs officials.‘The RSS: A Menace to India’ was the title of the book published in 2019. The opening lines of the introduction, where A.G. Noorani used a couplet, reflected what he described as the prevailing sentiment among Muslims in India today. In the same introduction, he referred to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru’s remarks at a Ministry of External Affairs officers’ meeting, documented by Foreign Secretary Gundevia.Nehru had warned that ‘the real danger to India was not communism, but Hindu right-wing communalism’," he said.During his speech, Ansari discussed Noorani's writings and his views on nationalism, identity and political developments in India. He also referred to Noorani's criticism of what he saw as a shift from civic nationalism towards cultural nationalism.“In recent years, we have experienced the emergence of trends and practices that dispute the well-established principle of civic nationalism and interpose a new and imaginary practice of cultural nationalism,” Ansari said.“It seeks to present an electoral majority in the guise of a religious majority and monopolise political power. It wants to distinguish citizens based on their faith, give vent to intolerance, insinuate otherness, and promote disquiet and insecurity,” he added.Ansari raised concerns over what he described as emerging trends that challenge the principle of civic nationalism.During his speech, Ansari said, “Some of its recent manifestations are chilling and reflect poorly on our claim to be governed by the rule of law. It’s a question that has to be answered. These trends need to be contested and contested legally and contested politically.”Reacting to Ansari's remarks, the BJP Scheduled Tribe Morcha said the statement brought what it described as Congress's “anti-Hindu politics” into focus. The BJP unit also referred to Rahul Gandhi's past remarks on Hindu groups and terrorism, alleging that such statements reflected a pattern in the party's political narrative."A remark from Nehru that Hamid Ansari highlighted, once again putting Congress’s anti-Hindu politics in the spotlight. Alongside Rahul Gandhi’s past remarks on Hindu groups and terrorism, that such statements reflect a pattern in the party’s political narrative," BJP said in a post on X.

NEW DELHI: BJP leader and former Union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu shared videos on X showing his detention by police after he protested with eggs and tomatoes as Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's cavalcade passed through Ludhiana.In the footage, Bittu could be heard saying, "throw, throw!" as police detained him. The video was posted with the caption, "Love to Bhagwant Mann from Punjabis."Bittu was detained by Ludhiana Police and taken to an undisclosed location.He stepped up his criticism of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, accusing the state government of failing to act against those allegedly involved in the attack on his convoy and the BJP's 'Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra'.Bittu alleged that the attack was linked to the drug trade in the state and claimed that no action had been taken against those responsible. He also challenged Mann to confront him directly, saying, "If Bhagwant Mann had the guts, he would have faced me. Today, the Chief Minister is making a narrow escape.""You have addicted all of Punjab to drugs. You are getting people attacked because you are colluding with drug traffickers.That is why you orchestrated an attack on me and the BJP yatra yesterday. I would not have had to come here today if action had been taken against those goons. However, no action was taken against them because they are the biggest drug lords," he added.He also urged the Sikh community's leadership to lodge a formal complaint over the alleged disruption of devotees travelling during the Viah Purab celebrations of Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Referring to the throwing of eggs on the road, he said, "Today, I want to appeal to Jathedar Sahib that a formal complaint be lodged.""The Viah Purab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji is being celebrated. People were laying down mats on the road; they were sweeping it clean so that no one would step on anything unclean or get a speck of dirt on them. The entire Sangat was proceeding to pay obeisance, but it was disrupted. Just imagine, eggs were thrown at the very spot on the road where the Sangat was traveling. I urge Jathedar Sahib to ensure a formal complaint is lodged," he said.He further appealed for those responsible to be removed from the Sikh community, saying, "Those responsible for this should be expelled from the Panth (Sikh community).""If the Chief Minister has the guts, let him come himself and face me. If we were to start doing the same thing, you would not be able to set foot in any state. The windows of all my vehicles were smashed yesterday; I only survived because I was in a bulletproof car," Bittu said.The development came a day after Bittu alleged that his cavalcade was attacked while he was travelling to Pathankot to attend a BJP yatra.He accused the AAP government of turning into a “gangster party” and alleged that police failed to take action during the incident."There was an attack on me. The DGP and the CM should be ashamed," he added.Bittu alleged that protesters surrounded his convoy, threatened to attack those inside and damaged the windows of the vehicles. He also claimed that some of the protesters were carrying weapons.The BJP's 'Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra' was launched across the state on Friday as part of the party's campaign to raise awareness about the drug menace. Bittu was travelling to Pathankot to participate in the campaign when he alleged that his convoy was attacked by around 500 people.BJP MP Raghav Chadha alleged that the Aam Aadmi Party was "scared" and attempting to target Bittu following the alleged attack on his cavalcade.

Article Title: Extremely speedy action by probe agency can create doubt: SC
Article Text:
The Supreme Court acquitted the RPF official, saying the CBI failed to prove that the intermediary accepted the bribe on his behalf.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: The speed at which CBI sprang into action on a bribery complaint and laid a trap within hours to catch a public servant could give rise to suspicion, which, Supreme Court said, could not be brushed aside and had to be examined.Finding fault with CBI's investigation, Justices Dipankar Datta and N K Singh acquitted the official in a two-decade-old case as he was not caught with the bribe money. It was an intermediary who accepted it and CBI failed to prove it was meant for the accused, SC said.The complaint made in 2005 alleged that the accused, working as a divisional security commissioner in Railway Protection Force , had demanded illegal gratification from subordinate officials for transfers and postings. CBI immediately lodged an FIR and laid a trap just hours later, catching the intermediary.The intermediary, who alleged that he accepted the bribe on behalf of the official, was given a pardon.SC said since the FIR was lodged on Aug 4, 2005, at 2pm and CBI decided to lay the trap on the same day, the agency must have verified the authenticity of the complaint before the trap was planned. "It is surprising that CBI started the investigation of a cognisable offence by way of verifying the complaint of bribery even before the formal FIR was lodged...The entire trap was arranged between 2 pm to 4.30pm. While the investigating agency cannot be faulted for organising the trap in such an extraordinarily speedy manner, it can raise certain doubts. The trial court, however, brushed aside the doubts raised by the appellant," the bench said.The court said criminality under Prevention of Corruption Act did not arise merely because money changed hands. "Before criminal liability can be fastened upon the public servant, the prosecution must establish by reliable evidence that the intermediary was acting under the authority, direction or for the benefit of the accused and that the demand itself was attributable to the accused. Mere receipt of money by a third person cannot automatically result in criminal liability being imputed to a public servant," it said.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court acquitted the RPF official, saying the CBI failed to prove that the intermediary accepted the bribe on his behalf. Justices Dipankar Datta and N K Singh acquitted the official in a two-decade-old case as he was not caught with the bribe money.

Article Title: Houthis, Saudis, Iran - and the future of Middle Eastern oil
Article Text:
Houthi fighters stand in front of what they say is a downed Saudi jet, at a location given as Yemen

What’s the latest Houthi offensive all about?

Why is this a serious headache?

Why now?

Why are Saudis in a jam?

What are the takeaways?

In a lightning offensive last week, Yemen’s Houthis took over much of the country’s Red Sea coast, threatening shipping in the vital sea lane that had emerged as an alternative to Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf. Houthis have been fighting a Saudi-led military coalition for a decade, although a 2022 UN-brokered truce halted their attacks on Saudi territory. But the Houthis’ latest move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark, adding another front to the wider US-Israel war against Iran. Here’s the lowdown on why the Houthis’ Red Sea threat matters, how this puts Saudi Arabia in a serious pickle, and what it means for the Iran war:The offensive saw Houthis take over key parts of Yemen’s Red Sea coast. This adds weight to the Houthi threat to shipping in the vital sea lane. In fact, Houthis had earlier declared a blockade of Saudi ships in the region. Now they can seriously enforce this. Their mere presence along the coastline will make shippers jittery and raise insurance costs.With Strait of Hormuz effectively locked up by Iran and US, Red Sea had emerged as a vital alternative route, especially for energy trade out of the region.Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline was working at full capacity, transporting around 7 million barrels of oil daily across the breadth of the peninsula to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. This was a crucial lifeline for the global energy trade that had been severely restricted following the outbreak of the Iran war in Feb. But that East-West pipeline was hit by a drone attack last week — blamed on Iran-backed Shia militias in Iraq — to coincide with the Houthi advance on the Red Sea coast. Both operations seem to have been coordinated to put the choke on Red Sea shipping, which has to pass through the narrow Bab el-Mandeb strait that Houthis can now theoretically shut down.The timing of all this is not a coincidence. Actually, when the Iran war began, among Iran’s proxies in the region, Houthis held back. But in July, following the state funeral of Iran’s former supreme leader Ali Khamenei, an Iranian plane carrying the Houthi delegation back to Yemen was threatened by Saudi Arabia. Riyadh did not want that plane to land, and bombed the airport in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital of Sanaa. But that plane landed anyway.Following the episode, Houthi rhetoric against the Saudis flared up. But the key development that may have pushed Houthis into action could be the American blockade of Iranian ports and shipping in Persian Gulf.By many estimates, that blockade appears to be working, and putting enormous pressure on the Iranian economy. Tehran is unable to push out its own oil, the Iranian rial has tanked, and Iranians have actually taken to saving eggs instead of hard cash. Plus, this is a strategy that plays into America’s strength — it can carry out a naval blockade for a far longer period than a continuous kinetic war against Iran.So, Iran, through the Houthi action, is sending the message that if oil can’t pass through Hormuz, any alternative routes, including through the Red Sea, will also be shut. In short, the energy trade in the region is handcuffed till the war is resolved.What do Houthis want? The Houthis’ main grievance is against the Saudis, whom they have been fighting since 2015. But, of course, as a member of Iran’s so-called ‘Axis of Resistance’, they are now being heavily supported by Tehran in terms of material and intelligence inputs. Especially since the Gaza and Iran wars have seen Tehran’s two main proxies in Hezbollah and Hamas take a huge battering. So, the Iranian Axis appears to be undergoing a recalibration, with Houthis and Iran-backed militias in Iraq taking a more leading role among the proxies. Ultimately Houthis want legitimacy. Their attacks against Saudi Arabia — they reportedly fired a drone at Mecca earlier this week — raise their profile. Their capture of the Red Sea coast gives them international attention. And these, in turn, see them emerge as the primary force in Yemen, instead of the internationally backed Yemeni transition govt. Obviously, all of this helps Iran.Because US has refused to directly intervene against Houthis this time. Washington is providing diplomatic and advisory support to Riyadh, but not much else. Saudis want missile and drone interceptors. But US stocks are running low, thanks to its war with Iran. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has similarly sought assistance from Egypt and UK. But no one is rushing military aid to Riyadh. Interestingly, even the recently inked Mecca Pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan hasn’t been activated.First, Houthis prove Iran’s Axis of Resistance is changing shape, with the Yemini militia taking a leading role. This has implications for both the Iran war, and security in Red Sea and Horn of Africa region. And second, alternative routes to Hormuz for energy transit, whether through sea or pipelines, are also not fully secure. They can be targeted by a host of Iran-backed militias in the region. This puts West Asia’s dominance in global energy supply under a serious cloud, perhaps forcing the international community to look for alternatives away from the region.
Article Summary: Houthis have been fighting a Saudi-led military coalition for a decade. The Houthis’ latest move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark. Red Sea had emerged as an alternative to Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf.

Article Title: 'Prisoner No. 626710 is Present': CBFC flags Umar Khalid film screening at IIIT-Hyderabad
Article Text:
Umar Khalid





HYDERABAD: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) objected to the proposed screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at IIIT-Hyderabad, saying screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless an exemption had been granted, according to news agency PTI reported.The documentary, "Prisoner No. 626710 is Present", directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, was proposed to be screened by a group of students at the institute's KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. Sources said the students have now decided to cancel the screening."Public screening of a documentary film that has not yet been certified by the CBFC is a violation of the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been sought under the Act," the CBFC posted on X.Tagging IIIT-Hyderabad, the CBFC said the institute's authorities "may take note for necessary action".The CBFC functions under the Union Information and Broadcasting Ministry.IIIT-H, however, distanced itself from the proposed screening, saying neither the institute nor any of its recognised student bodies had organised or hosted a screening of an uncertified film.In a statement, the institute said it "categorically clarifies that neither the Institute nor any of its recognised student clubs, cells or organisations has organised or hosted any screening of any film uncertified by the Central Board of Film Certification"."IIIT Hyderabad has established processes governing official events and activities on campus, and any claim attributing an unauthorised or unrelated activity to the Institute or its recognised student bodies is factually incorrect," it said.The institute said students and faculty from its large and diverse community may meet or interact with people in their individual capacities."Such personal interactions or visits, where they occur, should not be construed as Institute-organised events, nor do they represent the views or activities of the Institute," it said.The development comes days after a proposed screening of the same documentary at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) in Bengaluru was postponed following opposition from the RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP).The NLSIU screening, organised by its student-run Law and Society Committee, was scheduled for September 14 to mark Political Prisoners' Day and six years of Khalid's incarceration.The ABVP had demanded that the screening be cancelled, alleging that allowing it would amount to using the campus for political propaganda.The student committee later postponed the programme citing "logistical and security considerations". It maintained that it was not backing out because of pressure and said the screening would be held later in the trimester."Prisoner No. 626710 is Present" centres on Khalid, a former Jawaharlal Nehru University research scholar who was arrested in September 2020 in connection with the alleged larger conspiracy behind the northeast Delhi riots.Khalid has been charged under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and other provisions in the case and has remained in custody since his arrest.The invitation for the proposed IIIT-H screening said it was planned on the occasion of "Political Prisoners' Day".It also referred to the anniversary of the death of revolutionary Jatindra Nath Das, a comrade of Bhagat Singh who died after a prolonged hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929.
Article Summary: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) objected to the proposed screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at IIIT-Hyderabad. The documentary, "Prisoner No. 626710 is Present", directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, was proposed to be screened by a group of students at the institute's KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. Sources said the students have now decided to cancel the screening.

Article Title: 'Negotiate or face decisive war': Iran conveys terms to US for restarting talks, sets 7 conditions
Article Text:
Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei laid out the conditions that Iran sent to the US

Iran has formally conveyed its conditions to United States for ending the war, with its top official saying it has set out seven conditions for restarting negotiations while warning that it is also prepared for a “decisive war”.Iran’s supreme national security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei told Al Jazeera in an exclusive interview that Qatar had passed Tehran’s conditions to Washington and that Iran was awaiting US President Donald Trump’s response. “Our conditions are an end to the war on all fronts, the release of our frozen funds and an end to the naval blockade,” Rezaei said.“It is in Washington’s interest to accept these conditions. Trump’s threats will not achieve any results. We are prepared for a decisive war,” he added.In a separate post on X, he confirmed that it had announced seven conditions for starting negotiations with the US, saying Washington would have to accept Iran’s “rights and conditions” if it wanted to “escape the quagmire” and avoid becoming further entangled in the conflict.“It is in Washington’s interest to accept these conditions.Trump’s threats will not achieve any results. We are prepared for a decisive war,” Rezaei added.Meanwhile, Rezaei also told Al Jazeera that Iran was also preparing for the possibility of another US strike, describing it as “very much on the cards”. He said Tehran had changed its military planning and was now focused on US naval assets across the Gulf, the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.He claimed Iran had recently test-fired a multi-warhead anti-ship missile near a US vessel or aircraft carrier and warned that any future Iranian response would include US bases and American commercial interests in the region.At the same time, Rezaei said Tehran was pursuing diplomacy to bring the conflict to an end “as soon as possible”. Qatar and Pakistan have been involved in efforts to restart negotiations between Washington and Tehran after their earlier memorandum of understanding expired.On the nuclear issue, Rezaei said Iran had not decided to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, although he warned that further sanctions or a referral of its nuclear file to the UN Security Council “may push Tehran into withdrawing”.He also said Tehran remained open to an agreement with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz, saying the two sides had come within “a short step” of reaching a deal before it was shelved.The comments come as Washington weighs its next move in the conflict. Trump told Axios this week that he was facing a “big decision” over whether to resume major military action against Iran. “Do I want to go in and annihilate them [the Iranian regime] or do I not?” Trump had said, adding, “Anything could happen with me.”
Article Summary: Iran's supreme national security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei told Al Jazeera in an exclusive interview that Qatar had passed Tehran’s conditions to Washington. “Our conditions are an end to the war on all fronts, the release of our frozen funds and anend to the naval blockade,” he said. ‘We are prepared for a decisive war,’ he added.

The current round of fighting began in mid-July after strikes on Houthi-controlled Sanaa International Airport. The strikes came as an Iranian passenger plane carrying a senior Houthi delegation was returning from Iran.

Smoke seen near airport

Saudi Arabia says attacks were thwarted

Smoke rose near King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh after Yemen's Houthi rebels launched a large-scale attack on Saudi Arabia on Saturday. Two explosions were heard in the capital, while some flights were delayed.The Houthis said they targeted "sensitive targets" in Riyadh and a Saudi Aramco facility in Yanbu. The group said it used ballistic and cruise missiles and drones in the attacks.Saudi air defences later said they had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile targeting Riyadh.Videos showed a plume of smoke rising near King Khalid International Airport after the second explosion.Saudi authorities had earlier issued an aerial threat alert for Riyadh. The alert was reportedly the first such warning issued for the Saudi capital since tensions with the Houthis escalated.The Houthis reportedly targeted the fuel storage infrastructure at the airport triggering large plumes of smoke to rise up.There were no immediate reports of casualties or major damage in Riyadh.Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said the group had launched two major operations.The first targeted what he called "sensitive targets" in Riyadh. The second targeted a facility belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco in Yanbu, a major industrial and energy hub on the Red Sea coast."The two operations were successful," Sarea said.He claimed that large fires broke out at the targeted sites. The claims could not be independently verified.The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences intercepted the missile targeting Riyadh. It also said attacks on Baish, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu had been thwarted.Coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki said the attacks targeted "civilians and civilian objects". He also warned that Saudi Arabia would take "appropriate measures" to deter further attacks.The Houthis denied deliberately targeting civilians.Sarea said the attacks were in response to increased Saudi airstrikes on Houthi-held areas in Yemen. He vowed to continue what he called an "escalation for escalation" strategy until Saudi airstrikes stop and restrictions on Yemen are lifted.The latest attack marks a major escalation in the confrontation between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia.The current round of fighting began in mid-July after strikes on Houthi-controlled Sanaa International Airport. Article Title: 3 youths killed, 1 critical after speeding BMW crashes on Mumbai's Coastal Road, plunges off bridge
Article Text:
The car was travelling from Marine Drive towards Haji Ali when the driver allegedly lost control due to overspeeding.





MUMBAI: At least three people were killed and one critically injured after a BMW crashed on the Mumbai Coastal Road near Lotus Jetty on Sunday.The incident occured around 5.20am.According to police, the car was travelling from Marine Drive towards Haji Ali when the driver allegedly lost control due to overspeeding.The speeding vehicle crashed into a boundary wall before plunging off the bridge.The two deceased victims have been identified as Shanay Gajjal (21) and Dhirya Seth (17), while an unidentified 25-year-old man was also declared brought dead, according to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC).The fourth occupant, an unidentified male aged around 20, sustained severe injuries and is currently admitted in a critical condition in the hospital's trauma ward, the official said.Police have launched an inquiry into the incident.The Mumbai Coastal Road is a 10.58-km high-speed freeway connecting Marine Drive in south Mumbai to the Worli end of the Bandra–Worli Sea Link.
Article Summary: The BMW crashed on the Mumbai Coastal Road near Lotus Jetty on Sunday. The two deceased victims have been identified as Shanay Gajjal (21) and Dhirya Seth (17) The fourth occupant, an unidentified male aged around 20, sustained severe injuries and is currently admitted in a critical condition in the hospital's trauma ward.

Article Title: Out on bail, old enmity, 3-4 men in car: How pregnant YouTuber wife’s murder accused was hacked to death
Article Text:
Chithari Haribabu, recently released on bail, was hacked to death by unknown assailants.

'Old enmity'





HYDERABAD: About six months after he was arrested for allegedly killing his pregnant wife, who was also a YouTuber, Chithari Haribabu was hacked to death by a group of unidentified men at Rajarajendra (RR) Centre in Nizamabad on Thursday. He had been out on bail for the past two months.According to B Prasad, ACP, Nizamabad, 26-year-old Haribabu was intercepted by a group of men in a car near Rajarajendra Chowrasta at around 5pm. "Three to four people arrived in a car. One person got out, followed Haribabu and attacked him on the neck and head with a knife used for cutting coconuts," the ACP said. The victim suffered severe injuries and died on the spot. His body was shifted to the govt general hospital, Nizamabad, for postmortem.While police suspect old enmity to be the motive, they have launched an investigation to ascertain the facts. Investigators are also examining whether Haribabu's killing was linked to the murder of his wife, Vaishnavi. On March 17, Vaishnavi, who ran a popular YouTube channel, 'Vaishu Amma', was found dead at her residence in Madhapur village of Korutla mandal, Jagtial, when she was four months pregnant.Her family alleged that Haribabu strangled her and attacked her with a knife following a heated argument between them the previous night. Based on a complaint by Vaishnavi's father, police registered a murder case and arrested Haribabu after taking him into custody on the outskirts of Korutla.Police also booked his mother, Lakshmi, and brothers, Anand and Ashok, for alleged dowry harassment. Haribabu was subsequently released on bail in July."We suspect Vaishnavi's brothers' involvement in this murder but are yet to establish it. We have booked a murder case and are probing all angles to establish the identity of the accused," the ACP added.
Article Summary: Chithari Haribabu, 26, was hacked to death by a group of unidentified men. He had been out on bail for the past two months after being arrested for allegedly killing his pregnant wife, who was also a YouTuber. Police suspect old enmity to be the motive.

Article Title: Apple manager’s murder: 8 years on, 1 cop convicted, another let off
Article Text:
vivek tiwari murder by up police constable at saheed path gomti nagar , residence of vivek tiwari at new hyderabad aakash ganga hospital police constable and other people are gatherd at there residence

Daughters struggle to cope with father’s death

Dissatisfied with verdict, will appeal in higher court: Vivek’s wife





LUCKNOW: Eight years after a 38-year-old Apple area sales manager Vivek Tiwari was allegedly shot dead by two cops in Lucknow, a local court on Thursday convicted constable Prashant Chaudhary of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, while acquitting co-accused constable Sandeep Kumar . The quantum of punishment will be announced on Sept 21.District/sessions judge Malkhan Singh held Prashant Chaudhary guilty under the charges of IPC 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder).As per police chargesheet, Prashant was accused of IPC 302 (murder) and co-accused Sandeep of IPC 323 (voluntarily causing hurt).Soon after the judgement was pronounced, both the cops and their kin erupted in joy.Pranshu Agarwal, who represented Vivek Tiwar’s family, told TOI they will go through the detailed judgement and then file an appeal in the high court. “We are awaiting for the judgement copy in the case and also pronouncement of judgement on Sep 21,” said Agarwal.Vivek Tiwari, a resident of New Hyderabad colony, was driving his former colleague Sana Siddiqui to her home in his XUV around 1:30am on Sept 29, 2018. As they reached near Makdoompur outpost in Gomti Nagar Extension, bike-borne cops Prashant Chaudhary and Sandeep signalled them to stop.As Sana lowered the window pane to enquire about the reason, Sandeep hit her with a baton.Vivek did not stop and kept driving. At this, Prashant allegedly took out his service pistol and shot at Vivek, who had barely driven 0.5km ahead.The bullet hit Vivek and he rammed the vehicle on a divider. The two cops fled. Sana sought help from the police control room and took Vivek to Lohia Hospital where he died during treatment.An FIR against the two cops was lodged the next day and the chargesheet against them was filed on Dec 19, 2018. Prashant was charged with murder, while Sandeep was initially charged under Section 323.Vivek’s daughters, aged 15 and 20, still go numb on the mention of his tragic demise. Divyanshi, who was just 7 at the time of incident, had initially been told that her dad was away in Delhi and would return soon. But now the teen girl knows the reality. Priyanshi tries to console her younger sibling every time she breaks down. Divyanshi’s favourite possession is a family drawing she made years ago depicting Vivek, Kalpana, Priyanshi, and herself.Vivek wife Kalpana’s life has been consumed by grief. Every corner of her home is filled with memories of her husband. As she steps into her role as Officer on Special Duty at Nagar Nigam, she carries the weight of her husband’s absence. Kalpana’s brother, Vishnu, said, “He was always there for us, guiding us, helping us. Now, all we want is justice.”Kalpana Tiwari expressed strong dissatisfaction with the verdict and said she would challenge it before a higher court. Speaking after the judgment, she described the decision as disappointing and said the family had expected a harsher punishment.“We had been waiting for the court’s decision since morning and hoped that justice would be delivered. But we are disappointed with the verdict,” Kalpana said, according to the report. She questioned how a trained police constable could have made a mistake while firing his service weapon and maintained that her husband had been shot dead. Kalpana also questioned Sandeep Kumar’s acquittal, saying both constables were present at the spot and, in her view, shared responsibility for the incident.
Article Summary: Vivek Tiwari, 38, was driving his former colleague Sana Siddiqui to her home in his XUV around 1:30am on Sept 29, 2018. As they reached near Makdoompur outpost in Gomti Nagar Extension, bike-borne cops Prashant Chaudhary and Sandeep signalled them to stop. As Sana lowered the window pane to enquire about the reason, Sandeeps hit her with a baton. Vivek did not stop and kept driving.

Article Title: 'Ab nikaal ke bata gadi': A month before Gurgaon hit-and-run case, men chased, harassed Bhopal biker
Article Text:
In Bhopal, biker Abida Rana encountered a troubling situation when two men in a car relentlessly pursued her on Nabibagh Road





BHOPAL: Nearly a month before a woman biker’s hit-and-run incident in Gurgaon sparked widespread outrage, 23-year-old Bhopal-based biker, Abida Rana, had faced a similar ordeal in the city, with two men in a car chasing her for around 600-700 metres, abusing and repeatedly blocking her way.The ordeal took place on Aug 2 on Nabibagh Road, under Nishatpura police station limits. Abida had shared a video of the Bhopal ordeal on her Instagram handle on Aug 5, which is being widely circulated now.According to Abida, she was around 5 km from home when on the Nishatpura-Nabibagh stretch, two men crossing the road allegedly stopped their car in the middle of the road near the divider and began abusing her without any apparent reason.One of the men allegedly shouted, “Ab nikaal ke bata gadi.” With vehicles behind her honking, Abida said she was forced to move around the car from the left side.The men allegedly changed course and started following her, and repeatedly blocking her way.Abida said she became panicked and angry and told the men that the police station was only 1-2 km away and warned them that she would complain if they continued following and threatening her.When she tried to drive away, the men allegedly blocked her path from the right side as well. She then drove towards the police station, claiming the men continued chasing her and hurling abuses. They left just before the police station.Later, the men were called up to the police station and cops warned the men not to approach her again and made them write an apology before allowing them to leave. No FIR was registered as Abida had opted not to pursue a criminal case, cops said.
Article Summary: Bhopal-based biker Abida Rana, 23, faced a similar ordeal in the city. Two men in a car chased her for around 600-700 metres, abusing and repeatedly blocking her way. Abida had shared a video of the Bhopal ordeal on her Instagram handle.

Article Title: Abandoned pony limping through Kharagpur traffic rescued for veterinary care
Article Text:
A rescued pony, previously abandoned and struggling with severe health issues, was saved from the bustling traffic in Kharagpur





KHARAGPUR: A 7- to 8-year-old skewbald pony found limping through traffic on Kharagpur’s Malancha Road with severely overgrown hooves and other painful health conditions has been rescued and transported to an Animal Rahat sanctuary for veterinary care and rehabilitation. The rescue was carried out following action by People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals India (PETA India), with assistance from West Midnapore district magistrate Bijin Krishna; Superintendent of Police Papiya Sultana; Kharagpur sub-divisional officer Bhuvana Pranith Pappula; Kharagpur Animal Resources Development department deputy director Chinmoy Chakraborty; Kharagpur Town Police Station inspector-in charge Amit Kumar Mitra; and local animal advocate Sudebi Bhattacharya. The operation also received support from Members of Parliament June Maliah and Sayani Ghosh.The abandoned pony was suffering from severely overgrown and enlarged hooves, swollen fetlock joints, chronic osteoarthritis, and impaired mobility. Despite the animal’s evident distress, PETA India personnel faced resistance from certain locals, delaying rescue efforts. The pony was finally secured and taken for treatment after intervention by local authorities and the MPs.“This abandoned pony is yet another victim of the joyride industry. This rescue shows what can be achieved when authorities, animal protection groups, and citizens act together,” said Maliah. “I thank PETA India for never giving up on this pony and Animal Rahat for housing the pony and all the officials led by DM Bijin Krishna and SP Sultana for their prompt intervention in the rescue operation. I urge the public to help other ponies by choosing animal-free forms of entertainment. ”In Kolkata, PETA India continues to campaign for the protection of horses used to haul tourist carriages. In June 2026 alone, the group registered three FIRs involving neglected or distressed horses, including a foal found running frantically through active traffic, a horse with severely overgrown hooves rescued from the Hastings area, and a mare who died in the middle of traffic in Ekbalpore. Since 2024, at least 18 horses in the city have reportedly died or succumbed to injuries from road accidents and other causes.The Calcutta High Court has taken note of the poor condition of horses, the prevalence of unlicensed hackney carriages, and the abandonment of ailing animals. In an order dated May 9, 2024, it directed the state government to develop a proposal to rehabilitate horse-carriage owners so that replacing horse-drawn carriages, as done in Mumbai, can be considered. On July 7, 2026, PETA India appealed for horse-drawn tourist carriages in Kolkata to be replaced with heritage-style electric carriages.PETA India, whose motto reads in part that “animals are not ours to use for entertainment,” opposes speciesism, a human-supremacist worldview.
Article Summary: A 7- to 8-year-old skewbald pony was found limping through traffic on Kharagpur’s Malancha Road. The pony was suffering from severely overgrown and enlarged hooves, swollen fetlock joints, chronic osteoarthritis, and impaired mobility. The rescue was carried out following action by People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals India.

Article Title: Woman dies by suicide; family cites online gaming losses and emotional distress in UP
Article Text:
A 38-year-old woman died by suicide at her Lucknow residence on Wednesday evening (AI image)





LUCKNOW: A 38-year-old woman died by suicide at her residence in Sushant Golf City area on Wednesday evening, with her family attributing the death to severe emotional distress following losses linked to online gaming and the alleged pledging of jewellery without their knowledge.The woman, identified as Vibha Gupta, a resident of Patel Nagar, was found unresponsive inside a room of the house.Inspector Rajeev Ranjan Upadhyay said Vibha’s husband, Rajkumar Gupta , told investigators that she had developed an addiction to online gaming and had lost a substantial amount of money while playing. Family members also informed police that Vibha had allegedly pledged some of her jewellery without informing them. After Rajkumar learned about the financial losses and the jewellery being pledged, he asked her to stop playing online games, they said.According to the family, Vibha remained deeply distressed in the aftermath of the financial losses and related tensions. Police said Rajkumar and Vibha were at home when the incident occurred.Rajkumar, a retired Army personnel, is currently working as a head clerk at Bank of Baroda in Vibhuti Khand. Police recorded statements from family members and are collecting relevant information as part of the inquiry.Family members said Rajkumar was previously married to Sunita Gupta, who died during treatment at Command Hospital in 2000. He has two daughters from the first marriage, Khushboo and Nikki. Rajkumar married Vibha in 2004, and the couple have a 17-year-old son, Atharva.
Article Summary: The woman, identified as Vibha Gupta, a resident of Patel Nagar, was found unresponsive inside a room of the house. Her husband, Rajkumar Gupta, told investigators that she had developed an addiction to online gaming and had lost a substantial amount of money while playing. Family members also informed police that Vibia had allegedly pledged some of her jewellery without informing them.

Article Title: ‘They’re my family’: Bengaluru woman stops crowd from attacking men accused of kidnapping her
Article Text:
Locals attacked a car on Magadi Road, suspecting a kidnapping attempt





BENGALURU: High drama unfolded on Magadi Road Wednesday night after a group of locals allegedly thrashed several men and damaged their car, suspecting they were trying to kidnap a young woman.Six persons, including a nine-year-old girl, sustained injuries in the commotion.However, the alleged kidnapping took a dramatic turn when the woman intervened and told the crowd that the men were her own family members, including her father, who had come from Rajasthan to take her back home.Speaking to police who arrived at the spot, the woman said she had married a man from another caste despite her family’s opposition. She alleged that her family had recently traced her to Bengaluru and was trying to force her to return to Rajasthan.“I’ve married a man from another caste and my family was against it. Recently, we came here and my family somehow followed me,” she told police.A senior police officer said the woman was being requested to lodge a complaint against her family so that action could be taken.Meanwhile, the family’s vehicle was badly damaged after the crowd attacked it. The family members allegedly tried to flee the spot, ramming into other vehicles in the process, officials added.Of those injured, one woman with serious head injuries has been shifted to the ICU of a nearby private hospital, police added. Cops said they are yet to register a case. Suspects have been detained and the car used in the “kidnapping” seized, police said.
Article Summary: Six persons, including a nine-year-old girl, sustained injuries in the commotion. The woman said she had married a man from another caste despite her family’s opposition. She alleged that her family had recently traced her to Bengaluru and was trying to force her to return to Rajasthan.

Olympia Coffee House in Colaba had its food licence suspended due to hygiene violations
