Article Title: Rajkot man kills 5-year-old daughter, stores body in fridge; ends life
Article Text:
Police at the house where the murder-suicide took place in Hadida village of Amreli district





RAJKOT: A five-year-old girl was allegedly murdered by her father, who decked up her body and placed it in the refrigerator before taking his own life, in Hadida village of Amreli district’s Savarkundla taluka late on Wednesday night.Preliminary investigation and suicide notes recovered indicated that the 40-year-old man, Kishore Dhanak, took the gruesome step out of financial crisis stemming from investment in a construction site. He allegedly smothered his daughter Himanshi and then hanged himself to death in another room.Late on Wednesday night, Hadida sarpanch called the police, informing them about the deaths. When cops reached there, they found Dhanak hanging and three suicide notes on the cot.One of the notes mentioned that he had killed his daughter and placed the body in the refrigerator.His wife Manju had gone to her aunt’s house on Sept 14. When she returned the next day, she found the house locked. Dhanak told her on the phone that he was at a friend’s house in Mahuva and asked her to go to her parental home in Dadhia.On Sept 16, he told Manju that he had gone to Mahuva in adjoining Bhavnagar district to collect money and later asked her to start for home.When he did not contact her again till evening, she sent her brother Ghanshyam to check on them. Ghanshyam found the house locked and received no response despite calling out to them.Manju, her brother and father subsequently reached the house. After being alerted by a neighbour, the sarpanch was called and the door was opened.In one note, Dhanak referred to around Rs 7.25 lakh due to him from the construction project and said he had also invested personal loan money in it.In another note, he reportedly admitted to killing his daughter by covering her mouth and said he did so because he feared she would suffer without him. The third note contained an apology and, on its reverse side, reportedly stated that he had kept his daughter’s body in the refrigerator.Police also found that Dhanak had worn gloves on his hands and feet and covered his face with a cloth before taking his own life.Girl’s head covered with chunri, tulsi leaves placed in mouthPL Chaudhary, inspector, Savarkundla Rural police station, said when the girl’s body was recovered from the refrigerator, her father had placed tulsi leaves in her mouth, covered her head with a chunri and put a garland around her neck. “There were signs of some kind of celebration in the room where Dhanak was found hanging. The room had been decorated with colourful balloons and kites,” he said.Investigators are now examining whether Dhanak had celebrated an occasion with his daughter shortly before allegedly killing her, and are trying to establish what happened in the house before the tragedy.
Article Summary: Kishore Dhanak, 40, allegedly smothered his daughter Himanshi and then hanged himself to death in another room. He took the gruesome step out of financial crisis stemming from investment in a construction site. His wife Manju had gone to her aunt’s house on Sept 14 and found the house locked.

Article Title: ‘2 shots, sacked ex-colleague, financial dispute’: Inside Delhi HR professional’s killing
Article Text:
31-year-old HR professional Yuvraj Singh Manchanda

Family lost contact after Gurgaon meeting

Call records, CCTV led police to Anya

Body recovered from Gurgaon drain





NEW DELHI: Police are probing the killing of a 31-year-old HR professional who went to Gurgaon on September 6 to meet his former colleague Anya Vats, was shot twice inside his own car and his body was kept in the vehicle for at least seven hours before being dumped in a drain, while the accused fled to Uttarakhand.Police have arrested Anya Vats and her partner Sanyam Sachdeva, both from Gurgaon, in connection with the alleged murder and produced in court, which sent them to five days’ police custody.Yuvraj had gone to a restaurant in Lajpat Nagar around 4pm on September 6. His family said he had gone shopping with his sisters before visiting the restaurant. He later told them he had a meeting in Gurgaon and asked his sisters to take a cab home before leaving.According to the complaint, the family spoke to Yuvraj around 7pm, when he said he would return home by 10pm. His phone then appeared to be switched off and the family could not reach him.His sister approached Lajpat Nagar police on September 11, following which a missing-person FIR was registered.Investigators analysed call detail records, internet protocol data and CCTV footage and found that Yuvraj had last spoken to Anya.He had also told his family that he was going to Gurgaon to meet her.Both Yuvraj’s and Anya’s phones were switched off, prompting investigators to track Anya’s movements. She subsequently emerged as a prime suspect.Investigators later detected a new mobile number allegedly being used by Anya. Technical surveillance indicated that she was in Uttarakhand. A police team was sent there, where Anya and Sanyam were apprehended.Police said the two disclosed their involvement in the murder and told investigators that they had thrown Yuvraj’s body into a drain near their house in Gurgaon.The disclosure led investigators to Badshahpur police station in Gurgaon, where an unidentified body was found in a drain on September 10. The body was badly decomposed.Police showed photographs of the body to Yuvraj’s family, who identified him.Police suspect a financial dispute to be behind the killing. Anya had worked with Yuvraj in 2022 at another prominent real estate developer’s office and was currently unemployed. Police said she was sacked from the company and that some financial irregularities may have been the reason for her termination, though this is being verified. Sanyam was also unemployed.Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the killing, the alleged financial dispute, the exact roles of the accused and other aspects of the case, besides collecting forensic and technical evidence.
Article Summary: Yuvraj Singh Manchanda, 31, went to Gurgaon on September 6 to meet his former colleague Anya Vats. He was shot twice inside his own car and his body was kept in the vehicle for at least seven hours before being dumped in a drain. Police have arrested Anya and her partner Sanyam Sachdeva in connection with the alleged murder and sent them to five days' police custody.

Article Title: Rajasthan man dies after setting himself ablaze at Himachal Pradesh’s Jwalamukhi temple
Article Text:
The deceased has been identified as Ramdas, a resident of Jhalawar in Rajasthan. (File Photo)

(With Agency Inputs)





KANGRA: A man from Rajasthan died on Friday after allegedly setting himself on fire at the Jwalamukhi temple in Himachal Pradesh’s Kangra district, police said.The deceased was identified as Ramdas, a resident of Jhalawar in Rajasthan.According to police, the incident took place on Thursday evening when Ramdas visited the temple to pay obeisance. Ramdas died during treatment at Dr Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College and Hospital in Tanda on Friday morning, police said.Dehra SP Sandeep Dhawal confirmed the incident and said the matter is being probed.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Ramdas, a resident of Jhalawar in Rajasthan. He allegedly doused himself with petrol and set himself on fire, sustaining severe burn injuries. He died during treatment at Dr Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College and Hospital.

Article Title: Warden knew risks, still sent 8 students into Telangana lake for idol immersion, 6 drowned
Article Text:
Six inmates drowned at Pedda Kancharla lake during Ganesh idol immersion





HYDERABAD: A day after six inmates of Sirisha Memorial Charitable Trust drowned during Ganesh idol immersion at Pedda Kancharla lake in Patancheru, on Hyderabad’s outskirts, police arrested the hostel warden following demands from the victims’ families for strict action against him.During the investigation, police found that the warden, 53-year-old Varanasi Jay Prakash Rao, had taken the students to the lake for the immersion and directed them to enter the water. “He knew about the danger of sending them into the water and yet allowed them to go ahead, without taking any precautionary measures. The boys eventually drowned,” said an official of Patancheru police.At 8 am on Thursday, Rao was taken into custody and subsequently arrested under Section 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) of the BNS. Patancheru inspector M Ravinder told TOI that the accused was produced before a magistrate and later sent to judicial remand.Meanwhile, the postmortem examination of the six deceased — G Narasimha Raju, 22, A Uday Kiran, 18, R Ganesh, 19, B Sumanth Reddy, S Shyam Kumar, 17, and N Siddharth, 16 — was conducted at a local hospital amid tight security.The tragic incident, police said, occurred a little after 5.30pm on Wednesday when 15 boys from the charitable trust-run hostel reached Pedda Kancharla lake for immersion.The mood was celebratory and the boys eagerly carried the idol to the lake, even as the warden waited near the tractor that had transported the idol from the hostel to the immersion site.“Initially, eight boys got into the water with the idol. When one of them started to drown, he held the hand of another boy in an attempt to save himself. But instead, all of them lost their balance and fell into the water along with the idol,” said a class 8 student who was present at the site. He added: “While two of them eventually managed to come out safely, the six others drowned.”Alerted by students waiting on the lake shore, some hostel staff and locals rushed to the site and retrieved the bodies from the water. Eyewitnesses said an ambulance and police reached the spot nearly an hour later.Police initially believed that the deceased were orphans but later learnt that they were not. The hostel also housed children who were in the care of single parents and those from financially weaker families.“These six boys belonged to different parts of Telangana and AP and had been living at the hostel since many years. On receiving the news, their family members rushed to Patancheru late on Wednesday night and demanded action against Rao for his alleged negligence in allowing the students to enter the water,” said a source.
Article Summary: Six inmates of Sirisha Memorial Charitable Trust drowned during Ganesh idol immersion at Pedda Kancharla lake in Patancheru, on Hyderabad’s outskirts. Police arrested the hostel warden following demands from the victims’ families for strict action against him. The warden, 53-year-old Varanasi Jay Prakash Rao, was produced before a magistrate and later sent to judicial remand.

Article Title: UP man beheads sleeping wife over ‘affair’, walks into police station

A man allegedly beheaded his sleeping wife in Hardoi over suspected infidelity.

LUCKNOW: Suspecting his wife of having an affair, a man allegedly beheaded her while she was asleep at their rented house in Hardoi’s Islamnagar Tiliya locality early Wednesday, police said.The accused, identified as Parvez (34), was arrested after he reportedly walked into a police station and surrendered.The victim, Nagma (28), had been married to Parvez for nearly 12 years. According to police, the couple’s relationship had been strained for several months, with Parvez allegedly suspecting his wife of being in contact with another man on the phone. Frequent arguments reportedly took place over the issue.Investigators said Nagma was sleeping when Parvez allegedly attacked her with a sharp-edged weapon. Police said he repeatedly assaulted her before severing her head.The couple had been living in a rented house for the past one-and-a-half months after Parvez sold his ancestral property.Nagma’s sister, Sabbo, claimed that she had been subjected to prolonged physical abuse and threats by her husband. She alleged that Parvez had repeatedly threatened to slit Nagma’s throat in the days leading up to the murder.The family also alleged that some of Parvez’s relatives were present in the house when the crime took place.Nagma’s mother, Zahida, alleged that her daughter had faced repeated harassment and intimidation from her husband and in-laws.Police have sent the body for postmortem and launched an investigation. Officers are questioning Parvez, examining the family’s allegations, and attempting to recover the weapon allegedly used in the crime.

Article Title: Days after PM Modi’s school friend gets relief in land dispute, Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancels construction permission to BJP MLA’s company
Article Text:
Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancelled construction permission for Seven Eleven company.





BHAYANDER: The Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation on Wednesday cancelled the construction permission granted to Seven Eleven company, days after BJP MLA Narendra Mehta announced that his company would relinquish possession of the disputed land following the matter being taken up with Prime Minister Narendra Modi In another development, additional tehsildar Nilesh Gaund allowed a petition filed by 81-year-old Asgarali Vohra and ruled against Seven Eleven and other respondents. The order is expected to clear the way for Vohra’s name to be entered in the land records for the property currently in the possession of Seven Eleven, which had fenced off the plot with metal sheets.Vohra had alleged that Mehta and Swayam Builders had illegally encroached on the land at Navghar in Bhayander. He had been pursuing the dispute for around 15 years.On September 8, Vohra approached PM Modi, whom he described as his childhood friend from B N School in Vadnagar in Gujarat, and sought his intervention in the dispute. Soon after, Mehta announced that he would relinquish possession of the property and withdraw a complaint filed against Vohra.On Wednesday, Mehta issued a statement denying that he or his company had cheated anyone.He said the disputed land had been sold to Vohra in 1989 by Renol Lobo and five others. Lobo and the others later sold the land to Swayam Builders in 2011, he said.Mehta further claimed that Seven Eleven had purchased the property through duly registered transactions from Joseph Fernandes and Mukesh Parekh. He said the company decided to return the land to Mukesh Parekh and Mervin Fernandes after a dispute arose over the property.The BJP MLA maintained that surrendering possession and cancelling the transaction was a decision taken to end the dispute and did not amount to an admission of wrongdoing.
Article Summary: Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancelled construction permission for Seven Eleven company. BJP MLA Narendra Mehta announced that his company would relinquish possession of the disputed land. In another development, additional tehsildar Nilesh Gaund allowed a petition filed by 81-year-old Asgarali Vohra and ruled against Seven Eleven.
